record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README are provided, but the referenced RESULTS.md and result files were not read. Results below are limited to what the README states.
record.tranche_reason: The README says the project reproduces single-direction refusal mediation using a difference-in-means direction and ablation, and reports behavioral results. It also applies a weight-edit version of the ablation and re-tests the behavior after DPO.
record.gate_note: The README reports behavioral outcomes for the original, weight-edited, and DPO-restored checkpoints, including re-extraction and ablation of a direction. Direction-selection details and the repository's additional files are not treated as reported outcomes unless the README gives the result. It does not report an addition/steering experiment.
record.test_reason: The study reproduces the original recipe on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct: a difference-in-means direction (AdvBench vs Alpaca), held-out layer selection, ablation, then weight orthogonalization. It reports ASR and over-refusal. It then DPO-restores refusal and re-extracts and re-ablates the direction. This bears on V1, V2, V7, and on V3's robustness part.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Balanced DPO restores refusal (ASR 0.80 to 0.24, over-refusal 0.004), but it relocates refusal to a new single direction at L15 on every seed and run (9/9). Ablating that direction leaves no val refusal and gives ASR 0.83; the vulnerability moved rather than disappeared.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes a reproduction using harmful-minus-harmless last-token activations and held-out ablation-based layer selection. It additionally bakes ablation into weights, then trains with DPO and re-extracts the direction. This is a tool/reproduction repository, not an independently published study; only README-reported results are recorded.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports changes by DPO recipe and epoch count: harmful-only DPO has high over-refusal, while balanced DPO has over-refusal 0.004. The restored direction is reported at L15; base-model best layers are late-stack L21, 20, 22. The first rank to cross 0.8 varies between runs.
record.problems: Repository is only partially read here: the README points to RESULTS.md and additional result files that were not available for inspection. README notes n=100 rank-1 points are within one SE of the 0.8 threshold, and the first rank crossing 0.8 varies between runs. Over-refusal is reported, but broad general capability is not.
record.rows_left_out: The README mentions rank-1 results for re-sampled preference-set runs as 9 of 9 placing the direction at L15, but gives no separate per-run refusal or ASR values for those runs. Other rank-curve and layer-profile details are referred to RESULTS.md or figures without numerical values in the README.

untested.parts: Direction addition to induce refusal; general capability benchmarks (only over-refusal is measured); models other than Llama-3.2-3B.
Released models other than Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct; capability cost of the weight edit beyond over-refusal.
Whether prompt-based jailbreaks suppress the direction; adversarial training with ablation in the training loop (the restoration here is DPO on an orthogonalized checkpoint).
Affine or cone representations; multiple directions within one layer.
Training regimes other than DPO restoration; whether any recipe prevents a single removable direction from forming.

record.verdict_notes: This is a GitHub repository, not peer reviewed, and only the README was read (RESULTS.md was unavailable). ASR uses a Granite Guardian judge, while val refusal uses a substring judge. Rank-k means ablating directions from the top-k layers. All rank points have n=100 and are within about one SE of 0.8. The record linked DPO-recipe rows (r5–r12) to V1 and V3 by mistake: they measure restoration training, not the direction's causal role. I also corrected r13 from partial to observed.

versions.untested_parts: No direction-addition experiment is reported. Over-refusal is measured, but broad general capability is not.
Only the stated Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct setup is reported; performance across other released models is not tested.
The README reports one ablation-based attack and DPO restoration, not a range of jailbreak methods or a separate training-against-ablation robustness evaluation.
No affine or cone representation is tested; the reported evidence concerns single-direction ablation and rank-k attack curves.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
No language or model-variant transfer is reported.

Although DPO recipes are compared behaviorally, the README does not report direction-extraction comparisons across those recipes sufficient to test whether training choices determine whether a removable direction exists.
